seoDescription: Hurt in a car crash in Pittsfield Charter Township? The State Police recorded 1,143 crashes there in 2024, with 3 people killed and 29 seriously injured, and three of the county’s ten highest-crash intersections are on Carpenter Road. Covers who pays under no-fault, fault at the corridors and the freeway ramps, deer crashes, who owns the road, an Ann Arbor or Saline address on a township crash, and the 14A-1 District Court. Free review. (313) 406-7606.
tagline: A Pittsfield Township crash usually happens on a county road, a U.S. route, or a freeway ramp, and usually carries an Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti, or Saline address. The road owner, the police report, and the court follow from where it actually happened.

c.v: Carpenter runs north and south through the east side of the township, past big-box stores, shopping centers, apartment complexes, and bus stops. It crosses Packard, Ellsworth, and Michigan Avenue, and three of those intersections made the county’s top ten in 2024. In a 2026 request for state money to study the corridor, the township described Carpenter as one of the most dangerous roads in Washtenaw County for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers, with multiple pedestrian deaths in 2025. A 2025 road safety audit of Carpenter and Packard found numerous risks to people on foot and on bikes. The crashes on Carpenter are:

items.v: left turns across several lanes into shopping centers and side streets
vehicles leaving parking lots and apartment drives (MCL 257.652)
rear-end crashes in the queues at the signals
red-light and left-turn crashes at Packard, Ellsworth, and Michigan Avenue (MCL 257.650)
pedestrians crossing between signals to reach a bus stop or a store

c.v: Between US-23 and Ypsilanti, Washtenaw Avenue (M-17) is a five-lane commercial road with driveways on both sides and shopping centers at Hogback and Carpenter. Hogback at Washtenaw had 41 crashes in 2024, the third most in the county. The 14A-1 District Court sits on the same road. The crashes are:

items.v: left turns into and out of the shopping centers
lane changes into an occupied lane (MCL 257.642(1)(a))
rear-end crashes in the center-turn and right-turn lanes
drivers turning across a sidewalk into a business and striking a pedestrian or cyclist

c.v: Michigan Avenue, State Street, and Ann Arbor-Saline Road.

Michigan Avenue (US-12) runs southwest toward Saline past subdivisions, schools, and commercial strips, and meets Carpenter at the county’s eighth highest-crash intersection. State Street and Ann Arbor-Saline Road carry commuters into Ann Arbor past the I-94 interchanges. These are higher-speed roads with long gaps between signals. The crashes are:

items.v: head-on and crossover crashes on undivided stretches
left turns at unsignalized intersections and subdivision entrances
rear-end crashes behind turning vehicles
deer, especially at dawn and dusk in the fall

items.v: rear-end and lane-change crashes in the backups at the ramps

crashes in work zones

items.v: Carpenter, Packard, Ellsworth, State Street, Platt, Hogback, and the subdivision streets belong to the Washtenaw County Road Commission. A claim for a road defect requires written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1402, 691.1404).

I-94, US-23, US-12 (Michigan Avenue), and M-17 (Washtenaw Avenue east of US-23) belong to MDOT. A road-defect claim against MDOT requires written notice filed with the Court of Claims within 120 days (MCL 691.1404).

c.v: The PIP level is not the same as your liability limits.

Since July 2, 2020, Michigan drivers choose a PIP medical level for each policy: unlimited, $500,000, $250,000, $50,000 for some Medicaid enrollees, or an opt-out for some Medicare enrollees (MCL 500.3107c). That choice is separate from the liability limits that protect the other driver.

faqs.question: My address says Ann Arbor. Was my crash in Pittsfield Township?

answer.v: Possibly. Most township residents have an Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti, or Saline mailing address. The crash report names the jurisdiction, and the responding agency is a clue: the township’s Department of Public Safety in the township, the Ann Arbor police in the city. The answer decides who owns the road and which district court hears a small claim.

faqs.question: I was hit at Carpenter and Packard. Who is at fault?

answer.v: It depends on the signal, the lanes, and the turn. Carpenter and Packard had 39 crashes, 14 injuries, and a death in 2024, the only fatal intersection on the county’s top-ten list. Signal data and nearby store cameras usually decide fault, and both are lost quickly.

faqs.question: I hit a deer on Michigan Avenue. Do I have a claim?

answer.v: Your own no-fault policy pays your medical bills and lost wages. Your car is covered only by your own collision or comprehensive coverage. There is no claim for pain and suffering unless another driver caused the crash, for example by swerving into you.

faqs.question: A pothole on Carpenter Road caused my crash. Do I sue the township?

answer.v: No. Townships do not own roads. Carpenter is a county road, and written notice must reach the Washtenaw County Road Commission within 120 days. If the road is I-94, US-23, Michigan Avenue, or Washtenaw Avenue east of US-23, the claim is against MDOT, with written notice filed in the Court of Claims within 120 days.

faqs.question: I was walking to a bus stop on Carpenter and was hit. Who pays my medical bills?

answer.v: A no-fault policy in your household pays first. If there is none, you claim through the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan. Your claim for pain and suffering is against the driver.

faqs.question: How many crashes are there in Pittsfield Township?

answer.v: The State Police recorded 1,143 crashes in the township in 2024. 3 people were killed, 29 were seriously injured, and 215 crashes injured someone.

faqs.question: Is my PIP medical coverage the same as my liability limit?

answer.v: Not necessarily. Your liability limits protect the other driver if you cause a crash. Your PIP medical level is a separate choice on the same policy, and it decides how much of your own medical care no-fault pays.
